contentHtml:
Do not compare the totals. First, break every quotation into the same line items. Second, match the material specifications (board grade, laminate thickness, hardware brand) and the measurement basis. Third, read the exclusions, payment terms and warranty. Only then compare prices. When you negotiate, negotiate on scope and specification, not just the rate, so you save money without quietly downgrading quality.

By the time most Gurgaon homeowners are ready to hire, they are holding three or four quotations for the same apartment, and the totals can be ₹5–10 lakh apart (our guide to interior design cost in Gurgaon shows what typical budgets look like). The lowest quote is rarely the cheapest home, and the highest is not automatically the best. The difference is almost always in what each quote measures, specifies and leaves out. This guide shows you how to read a quotation the way a designer does.

Why Two Quotes for the Same Home Can Differ by Lakhs

  • Different materials hidden under the same name. “Plywood wardrobe” can mean moisture-resistant commercial ply or boiling-water-proof marine ply.
  • Different measurement methods. One firm charges per sq ft of wardrobe face, another per running foot, a third as a lump sum.
  • Different scope. One includes painting, electrical and false ceiling; another prices only the woodwork.
  • Different allowances. “Lights as per client selection” or “tiles up to ₹80 per sq ft” leaves the real cost open.

The Anatomy of an Interior Design Quotation

A good quotation, often called a BOQ (bill of quantities), is organised room by room or trade by trade. Each line should tell you what is being made, from what, how big, at what rate and for how much.

SectionWhat a clear quote shows
Design & 3DNumber of 3D views, revision rounds, working drawings; whether the fee is separate or adjusted
Modular kitchenCarcass and shutter material, finish, hardware brand, countertop, appliances in or out
Wardrobes & storageArea or running feet, internal accessories, loft units, shutter type
False ceiling & lightingBoard brand, area, profile lights and fixtures (supplied or allowance)
Electrical & plumbingPoints added or shifted, wire and switch brand, fixtures
Civil & flooringDemolition, new walls, tiling, waterproofing
Painting & finishesPutty and primer coats, paint brand and type, texture or wallpaper areas
Loose furniture & décorSofa, beds, dining, curtains, rugs; item-wise or allowance
Taxes & termsGST, payment schedule, timeline, warranty, exclusions

Step 1: Check the Measurement Basis

Before anything else, find out what the rate is multiplied by. Wardrobes are usually priced per sq ft of the front face (width × height), kitchens per running foot or per unit, and false ceilings per sq ft of ceiling area. A “₹1,400 per sq ft” wardrobe and a “₹1,650 per sq ft” wardrobe are not comparable if one includes the loft and the other does not.

Also check whether any overall figure is based on carpet area or super area. A per-sq-ft rate on super area can look cheaper while delivering less.

Step 2: Match the Specifications Line by Line

This is where most of the price difference hides. Put the specifications side by side, and ask any firm that is vague to fill in the blanks. If you are also weighing factory-made against site-built work, read modular vs custom furniture for Gurgaon flats first, since it changes which specifications matter.

ItemWhat to look forWhy it matters
Carcass boardBWP (IS 710) in kitchen and wet areas; MR (IS 303) acceptable in dry areas; board brand namedMoisture resistance and life of the unit
Board thicknessTypically 18 mm for carcass, 6–8 mm for back panelsThinner boards sag and loosen over time
Laminate / finishBrand and thickness (0.8 mm vs 1 mm); acrylic, PU, veneer or membrane specifiedScratch resistance and appearance
Edge banding2 mm PVC or ABS, machine-appliedPrevents moisture entry at edges
HardwareNamed brand for hinges, channels, lift-ups; soft-close statedThe part you use every day and replace first
CountertopStone type, thickness, edge profile, sink cut-outsLarge cost swing between granite, quartz and marble
False ceilingGypsum board and channel brandCracking and sagging risk
PaintingPutty coats, primer, number of finish coats, paint brand and range“Painting” can mean one coat or five
ElectricalWire and switch brand, number of new pointsSafety and a common source of extras

Step 3: Read the Exclusions and “Client Scope”

Exclusions are where a low quote often catches up with you. Look for lines such as “appliances by client”, “lights, fans and chimney excluded”, “civil and debris removal extra”, “society charges extra” or “site protection not included”. Add a realistic cost for every exclusion to that quote before comparing it with a more complete one. Our guide to hidden costs in interior design projects lists the usual suspects.

Step 4: Compare Payment Terms, Timeline and Warranty

  • Payment schedule: stages should follow work progress. Be cautious of anything above roughly half the value before material reaches site.
  • Timeline: a start date, a handover date and what happens if either slips.
  • Warranty: what is covered (carcass, hardware, finish), for how long, and who you call.
  • Change orders: how extra work will be priced once the project starts. Ask for rates to be locked for the project duration.
  • GST: inclusive or exclusive, and whether the firm is issuing a proper tax invoice.

For a broader checklist of what to raise before you sign, see our 10 questions to ask before signing with an interior designer.

Putting It Together: A Sample Comparison Sheet

Here is how three wardrobe quotes for the same 3BHK might look once normalised. The cheapest headline rate turns out to be the most expensive like-for-like option.

Line itemQuote AQuote BQuote C
Headline wardrobe rate₹1,350 / sq ft₹1,650 / sq ftLump sum
BoardMR ply, brand not namedBWP ply, brand namedMR ply, brand named
Laminate0.8 mm1 mm, brand named1 mm
Hardware“Standard”Named brand, soft-closeNamed brand, soft-close
LoftsExtraIncludedIncluded
Internal accessoriesExtraIncludedPartly included
Adjusted like-for-like costHighest once upgrades addedMidLowest, but check timeline and warranty

Illustrative example. Build your own sheet in a spreadsheet with one row per line item and one column per firm.

Red Flags in an Interior Design Quotation

  • A single total with no room-wise or item-wise break-up.
  • Materials described only as “good quality”, “standard” or “premium” with no brand or grade.
  • Large allowances (“lights as selected”) that make the total look smaller than it is.
  • A very large advance with no link to design or site progress.
  • No written timeline, no warranty and no mention of GST.
  • Pressure to sign quickly for a “this week only” discount.

How to Negotiate an Interior Design Quote Without Cutting Quality

  1. Normalise first, negotiate second. Show each firm the specification you want and ask them to requote to it. You are now negotiating on price for the same thing.
  2. Negotiate scope, not just rate. Moving loose furniture or décor to a second phase often saves more than a 5% rate cut.
  3. Value-engineer the invisible, protect the daily-use. Internal carcass finishes can be simpler; hinges, channels and kitchen countertops should not be.
  4. Trade payment terms for price. Faster, reliable milestone payments are worth something to a firm. Use that, rather than a larger upfront advance. If you are considering finance, read how no-cost EMI for interior design really works first, since some plans pay the designer in full upfront.
  5. Lock rates for changes. A good deal on day one means little if extra work is billed at open rates.
  6. Get every concession in writing as a revised quotation, not a verbal promise.

faqs.question: How do I compare interior design quotations?
faqs.answer: Break each quotation into the same line items, match material specifications and measurement methods, add the cost of any exclusions, then compare payment terms, timeline and warranty before comparing the final price.

faqs.question: How can I negotiate an interior design quote in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: Ask every firm to requote to the same specification, reduce or phase the scope rather than just pushing the rate, offer reliable milestone payments in exchange for a better price, and get rates for future changes locked in writing.

faqs.question: What should an interior design quotation include?
faqs.answer: Room-wise line items with materials, brands, dimensions, rates and amounts, plus design scope, GST, a payment schedule, timeline, warranty and a clear list of exclusions.

faqs.question: Why is one interior quote much cheaper than another?
faqs.answer: Usually because of lower-grade materials, unbranded hardware, a different measurement basis, or items moved into exclusions and client scope. Once normalised, the gap often shrinks or reverses.

faqs.question: How much advance should I pay an interior designer?
faqs.answer: Keep the advance modest and tie further payments to progress such as design sign-off, material delivery and installation. Be cautious of paying more than about half the project value before material reaches site.
